# Timbre translation handoff

<!-- Generated by tools/l10n/report.py. Edit the template in that script, not this file. -->

This is the brief for whoever translates Timbre: people, or GPT run as described in [TRANSLATING-WITH-GPT.md](TRANSLATING-WITH-GPT.md) (with a terminology sheet from [GLOSSARY-TEMPLATE.md](GLOSSARY-TEMPLATE.md) and a human review of legal, permission and funnel text). The English is the source. Everything on this page and in the TODO files is generated from the code and the curriculum: the iOS workflow warns on every run while anything is missing, and fails when this page is out of date (see *For developers*). A string a locale lacks shows in English.

## Launch-critical first

Every launch-critical string is translated in every locale.

## What to translate

One file per language: `tools/l10n/todo/<locale>.json` (for example `tools/l10n/todo/de.json`). Each line of `strings` is one string: the launch-critical ones first (above), then the rest in the order a new user meets them: permission prompts, onboarding, the paywall and the tuner, then the lessons in course order. Its fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `table` | Where it ships: `Localizable.strings` (app interface), `Learn.strings` (lessons), `AppShortcuts.strings` (Siri phrases), `InfoPlist.strings` (system permission prompts), `Localizable.stringsdict` (plurals). |
| `key` | The identifier. Never change it. For interface strings it is the English itself. |
| `source` | The English to translate. |
| `context` | Where the text appears and what it does (a code comment, or the course, unit, lesson and step). |
| `where` | The code location, for a developer answering a question. |
| `layout` | Present when the text sits somewhere tight: `one line`, `small label`, `control label`, `shrinks to fit`. |
| `max_length` | Aim for at most this many characters. For lessons it is the limit the English is written to; for interface strings it is a soft limit from the layout. Longer text shrinks or truncates. |
| `launch` | Present on launch-critical strings, which come first: `legal`, `permission`, `voiceover` or `funnel` (see *Launch-critical first*). |
| `status` | `new`; `changed` (the English was edited: start from `previous.translation`); `rejected` (a translation failed a check: `problem` says why, and the text is in `translation` or `previous.translation`). |
| `translation` | **Your text goes here.** Leave it empty to skip a string. |

Rules the import checks (a translation that breaks one is kept out and listed again as `rejected`):

- Keep every format argument: `%@`, `%lld`, `%d`, `%lf`, `%.1f` and their count and order. To reorder, use positional forms: `%2$@ … %1$lld`. Keep `%%` (a percent sign) as it is.
- Keep named tokens exactly: `${applicationName}`, `${instrument}`, `${key}`, `${bpm}`.
- Lessons: keep every number, `♯`, `♭` and line break (`\n`) of the English. Note letters stay as in the English, except that German lessons write H for B natural and B for B flat (a German `B♭` becomes `B`; the check knows this).
- Keep the brand names Timbre and Timbre Pro, game names the English capitalizes (Bullseye), and song titles that are names. Lyric credits (a name and a year) are usually kept as they are.
- Voice: warm, direct, second person. Match the register the app already uses in your language (see its `Localizable.strings`) and keep it consistent. No exclamation marks or emoji the English doesn't have.
- Plurals (`Localizable.stringsdict`): put a JSON object in `translation` with the forms your language uses, e.g. `{"one": "%lld Minute", "other": "%lld Minuten"}`.

Reuse what is already translated: the app's current tables are in `ios/Timbre/Resources/<locale>.lproj/` (`Localizable.strings`, `Learn.strings`), and the delivered lesson translations in `tools/l10n/learn/<locale>.json`.

## How to deliver

1. Fill the `translation` fields of `tools/l10n/todo/<locale>.json`. Partial files are fine.
2. Send the file back (or commit it on a branch). Keep the file name and the JSON structure.
3. A developer imports it (below). Anything rejected comes back in the next TODO file with the reason.

Formats used in the repository, for reference:

- `tools/l10n/translations/<locale>.json`: `{"Localizable.strings": {"English key": "translation"}, "AppShortcuts.strings": {…}, "InfoPlist.strings": {…}}`, the interface translations `apply.py` merges.
- `tools/l10n/learn/<locale>.json`: `{"L0a1b2c3d4e": "translation"}`, the lesson translations `apply_learn.py` writes. Lesson keys are a hash of the English, so an edited sentence gets a new key.

## For developers

```sh
python3 tools/l10n/report.py                      # regenerate the TODO files, pending.json and this page
python3 tools/l10n/report.py --import tools/l10n/todo   # merge filled TODO files, apply, regenerate
python3 tools/l10n/report.py --check --strict     # what CI runs: fails when this page is out of date
python3 tools/l10n/critical.py --baseline         # what CI runs: fails on a new untranslated critical string
python3 tools/l10n/shipping.py                    # coverage per locale, and the languages that ship
python3 tools/l10n/lessons.py --strict             # full applied lesson coverage in all 48 targets
```

`--import DIR` reads every `<locale>.json` in DIR (the TODO format), checks each translation, merges the good ones into `tools/l10n/translations/<locale>.json` and `tools/l10n/learn/<locale>.json`, then runs the two apply scripts and regenerates the handoff. By hand, the apply steps are:

```sh
python3 tools/l10n/apply.py tools/l10n/translations   # interface tables, every locale
python3 tools/l10n/apply_learn.py                     # lesson tables, the lesson languages
```

Run `report.py` after adding or editing English (a new `Text("…")`, a curriculum change) and commit `tools/l10n/todo`, `tools/l10n/pending.json`, `tools/l10n/source` and this page with the change. The core job of the iOS workflow (`.github/workflows/ios.yml`) runs `report.py --check --strict` on every run: it prints a warning annotation with the per-locale counts, adds the table to the job summary, publishes fresh TODO files with the core results (branch `ci-results/core`, folder `l10n`), and fails when the committed handoff is out of date.

The same job runs `critical.py --baseline`: a legal, permission or VoiceOver string that a shipped locale lacks and that `tools/l10n/critical-baseline.json` doesn't list fails it. Deliver the translations, or record the gap with `python3 tools/l10n/critical.py --write-baseline` (the diff shows the reviewer which English goes out). The App Store upload (`apple-delivery.yml`) allows no gap at all; only an internal TestFlight build, which can't be submitted for review, may skip that check.

Which languages ship is the owner's decision: `CFBundleLocalizations` in `ios/project.yml`, every `.lproj` today. `python3 tools/l10n/shipping.py --min 95 --apply` ships only the locales with at least 95 % of the interface translated (add `--critical` to also require every launch-critical string), and `--all --apply` ships every one again. The translations stay in the repository either way. The delivery workflow's `ship_min_coverage` input applies a bar to one upload without committing it.

Interface strings are found by `tools/l10n/swiftstrings.py`, a scanner that reads Swift without Xcode. It infers the type of each interpolation (`%lld` for Int, `%@` for text); when a new string's key carries `key_check`, the inferred specifier is a guess. Confirm it with Xcode's export: run the *Localization export* workflow (`l10n.yml`) and pass its `en.xliff` with `--xliff`.

Stale entries: 159 keys that some locale still holds have no English in the app any more (5,810 locale-key pairs; the keys are listed under `stale` in `tools/l10n/todo/index.json`). They are harmless, and they are where `changed` entries find their old translations.
